source.snippet: We are currently dealing with a massive wave of AI bot and scraper traffic (GPTBot, ClaudeBot, Bytespider, curl, etc.) hitting our standard CloudPages — experiencing around 20 million hits recently. Because these requests load successfully and return a standard 200 OK, they are rapidly consuming our Super Message budget. We are actively working on mitigation strategies, but our infrastructure has a mixed setup (self-hosted and delegated domains) which brings up a few challenges.

problem_statement: Marketing Cloud / CloudPages customers on metered 'Super Message' plans are losing paid quota to AI crawlers and bots that return 200 OK, with no built-in Salesforce mechanism to block them without also disrupting legitimate traffic on mixed self-hosted/delegated domain setups.
target_segment: Salesforce Marketing Cloud administrators and agencies managing CloudPages for mid-to-enterprise brands on metered Super Message contracts.
notes: Buyer is paying for metered Salesforce Super Messages — 20M bot hits translates directly to wasted budget. Business context is explicit (enterprise MarTech stack). Poster is actively seeking paid/technical mitigations. A managed bot-filtering proxy or Cloudflare-worker pattern pre-configured for CloudPages self-hosted domains could be productized as a service or SaaS add-on. Willingness-to-pay is high given the direct cost leakage.
